content: Cumulina was a mouse born on December 3, 1997, and she lived until May 5, 2000. She holds the distinction of being the first animal cloned from adult cells that successfully survived to adulthood. Her cloning was achieved using a method known as the Honolulu technique, which was developed by the research team led by Dr. Ryuzo Yanagimachi, referred to as Team Yana. This groundbreaking work was conducted at the former campus of the John A. Burns School of Medicine at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. Cumulina was a brown-colored Mus musculus, commonly known as the house mouse. Her name, Cumulina, was derived from the cumulus cells, which are the cells that surround the developing ovarian follicle in mice. In the Honolulu cloning technique, the nuclei from these cumulus cells were transferred into egg cells that had been stripped of their original nuclei. Unlike other mice cloned in the Yanagimachi laboratory, which were identified only by numbers, Cumulina was given a unique name. She was able to produce two healthy litters of offspring before being retired from breeding after the second litter. Cumulina's preserved remains are now housed at the Institute for Biogenesis Research laboratory in Honolulu, Hawaii, which is part of the John A. Burns School of Medicine. Additionally, some of her descendants have been displayed at the Bishop Museum in Honolulu and the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago, Illinois.
